meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of South Africa (Unitary National Jurisdiction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Roman-Dutch civil-law heritage, English common-law influence, African customary law, constitutional supremacy)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: South Africa-United States Income Tax Treaty (1997, in force)
South Africa-United Kingdom Income Tax Treaty (2002)
African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Agreement
SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 71 of 2008 as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 (beneficial ownership register, effective 27 December 2024); Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004; CIPC Beneficial Ownership Directive and FIC Guidance Notes; FATF Recommendations as applied through the Eastern and Southern Africa Anti-Money Laundering Group.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in shareholder's country of residence / South African Commissioner of Oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by competent authority of country of origin; non-Hague states: consular legalization at South African High Commission/Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each shareholder and director (bank statement or utility bill, not older than three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank, utility provider, or municipal authority; sworn English translation if not in English
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for foreign-issued documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the South African incorporation agent and tax representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and companies-registry extract of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization plus sworn English translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the foreign corporate shareholder authorizing incorporation of ZA_PTY_LTD and director appointment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporation's board and company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter evidencing source of funds for the founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct bank letterhead with notarization/apostille; bank-to-bank SWIFT confirmation acceptable for FIC KYC

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory under Section 21A of the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (as amended by Act 22 of 2022) and FIC Directive 6. Prior to incorporation, each substantive UBO (5% or more) and every proposed director must be screened against: (i) the FIC domestic politically exposed persons (PEP) list; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iii) the South African national terrorist and related activities list under POCDATARA Act 33 of 2004; (iv) the OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions list for all USD-denominated settlement rails (Amazon Pay, Stripe, Airwallex); and (v) the EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists. Adverse hits require a written enhanced due diligence report, source-of-funds explanation, and, where applicable, prior FIC approval. Screening records must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services Portal (eservices.cipc.co.za) operated by the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in any of South Africa's official languages, all of which use the Latin alphabet. The name must be expressed in Latin-script letters and Arabic numerals, must be distinctive and not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, must not be offensive, and must be followed by the suffix 'Proprietary Limited' or its abbreviation '(Pty) Ltd'. Foreign or transliterated names must indicate the legal form and must not falsely imply connection with the state, a regulated profession, or a protected mark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: any offensive or ethnically/religiously inflammatory expression
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name is valid for 180 days and may be extended once for a further 180 days by lodging a renewal application through the CIPC e-Services Portal before expiry. If the name is rejected, the applicant may: (1) submit a written reconsideration request to the CIPC Registrar's Name Committee within 20 business days of rejection, with supporting submissions distinguishing the proposed name from conflicting registered names; (2) apply to the Companies Tribunal under Section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 for a determination that the proposed name satisfies Section 11; and (3) simultaneously file a fresh name-reservation application with alternative names to preserve the incorporation timetable. Urgent applications may be noted in the portal's escalation queue, but statutory timelines remain binding.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for a non-licensed, e-commerce-only (Pty) Ltd provided the service provider offers a genuine physical street address in South Africa where statutory notices and legal process can be served during normal business hours. Purely postal or non-premises virtual addresses are prohibited under Section 23 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. Banks and payment providers may impose additional physical-presence expectations at onboarding.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: approximately 5-8% annual probability for a compliant, non-licensed Amazon FBA entity filing timely CIPC annual returns and SARS tax declarations. The likelihood rises above 30% if the entity relies on an unverifiable virtual address, shows unexplained foreign remittances, undergoes repeated director or address changes, or is flagged in FIC risk-based supervision.

Accredited tax practitioner / accounting officer fee for coordinated CIPC and SARS filings and FIC risk assessment
Notarization and certified copies - passport, proof of address, shareholder resolution (three documents)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss. 13 (incorporation), 14 (application for registration), 19 (legal personality), 66 (directors), 69 (consents), 70-75 (disqualification and proceedings); Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 (beneficial ownership register obligations)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), 77 Meintjies Street, Pretoria; online via CIPC e-Services portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1A standard MOI for a private company)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a (Pty) Ltd; no escrow or trust account pre-incorporation is mandated. Shares may be no-par value and issued for cash or in-kind consideration, including a subscription price as low as R0.01 per share.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the inaugural board of directors, effective upon incorporation, as follows: 1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION: each subscriber hereby subscribes for 100 no-par value ordinary shares at R0.01 per share, payment in full upon allotment. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: the registered office is fixed at [Registered Office Address], South Africa, and notice shall be filed with CIPC. 3. DIRECTORS: [Director A] and [Director B], having consented in writing, are appointed as first directors under section 66. 4. IMPLEMENTATION: the directors are authorized to file the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1), adopt the standard MOI, procure SARS registrations, open bank accounts, and execute ancillary acts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Company Name with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal (biz.cipc.co.za), Company Name Reservations module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in or register a new CIPC e-Services user account; complete Form CoR 9.1 specifying up to four preferred names in descending order of preference; pay the non-refundable reservation fee of ZAR 50 electronically via payment deposit application or card; await CIPC adjudication against the names register and trademarks. The reservation is valid for six months and extensions may be applied for before expiry.
required_dossiers: CoR 9.1 Name Reservation Application
Copy of applicant identity document or passport
Trademark consent letter, if the proposed name contains a mark owned by a third party
Electronic payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusing similarity with an existing company or trademark, file an objection under the Companies Regulations 2011 or simply request re-adjudication with an amended distinctive prefix/suffix on the same application; CIPC permits resubmission of alternative names without a new reservation fee where the original application is still active.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal, Company Registration transaction (CoR 14.1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form CoR 14.1 with the proposed company name and reservation number; attach the signed and dated MOI, which may be the standard CoR 15.1A adjusted for the issued shares and director quorum; upload verified identity copies and consent-to-act documents of each director; pay the prescribed incorporation fee of ZAR 175; submit electronically. CIPC processes the application and issues the electronic Certificate of Incorporation upon acceptance.
required_dossiers: CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation
CoR 15.1A Memorandum of Incorporation signed by each incorporator
Certified copy of identity document or passport of each director and incorporator
Written consent to act as director for each appointee
Physical registered office address and postal address details
Completed CoR 14.1A (translation affidavit) where a director is a foreign resident and does not hold a South African identity number
Proof of payment of the incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC queries the application for incomplete director consents, address defects, or unpaid fees, cure the deficiency through the CIPC e-services interaction channel and resubmit within the stated action window; if rejected, amend the CoR 14.1, pay any resubmission charge, and re-file within five business days; no loss of name reservation occurs if the reservation remains valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and File Beneficial Ownership Particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal, Company Document Request and Beneficial Ownership Register modules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3) and the registered MOI from the CIPC company document repository; update the register of members; within ten business days after incorporation, file the beneficial ownership particulars using Form CoR 45.1 and CoR 45.2, disclosing every individual who directly or indirectly holds or exercises effective control of the company, including shareholding thresholds and control structure.
required_dossiers: CoR 14.3 Certificate of Incorporation
Registered Memorandum of Incorporation
CoR 45.1 Beneficial Ownership Declaration
CoR 45.2 Beneficial Ownership Register filing
Shareholder and control chain documentation sufficient to establish each beneficial owner, including percentage ownership and control rights
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the beneficial ownership filing is rejected for incomplete UBO percentage breakdowns or missing control particulars, correct the register and resubmit electronically; no additional incorporation fee applies; late filing triggers administrative penalties, so a curative submission should be made immediately upon CIPC notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Taxation with SARS (Income Tax, VAT, PAYE, UIF, Customs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS), eFiling portal (sarsefiling.co.za)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Take advantage of the automatic alignment between CIPC and SARS via the Integration of Tax and Company Registration System (ITRS); verify the company's income tax profile within 21 business days of incorporation; complete VAT registration on the eFiling portal if the company's taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed ZAR 1 million in any 12-month period, which applies to a general Amazon retail business scaling revenue; register for PAYE and UIF immediately upon hiring any employees; obtain a Customs Code if goods are to be imported into the SACU area for FBA inventory; appoint a SARS appointed tax practitioner or complete the electronic registration under the SARS 640s process where applicable.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and registered MOI
Identity documents of all directors
Bank account confirmation letter and bank details
Estimated turnover forecast or signed commercial agreements with marketplaces for the next 12 months
Proof of physical business location/lease agreement
SARS eFiling access request and organization link (where a practitioner files)
Power of attorney (SARS 64s) if a tax representative is appointed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS does not auto-populate the company's profile from CIPC, lodge a Change of Registered Particulars (RA30 form) or raise a manual tax registration enquiry via the SARS branch booking system; if the VAT application is queried on turnover evidence, submit marketplace statements or bank statements evidencing transaction volumes; escalation to the SARS service manager is available for registrations still pending after 15 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Incorporation Operational Registration (Bank, Municipal and Labour)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African banking institutions, local Metropolitan Municipality trading licence office, and Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account with FICA-compliant documents, appointing signatories by board resolution; verify municipal zoning and obtain a Business (Trading) Licence under the Business Act 71 of 1991 or relevant municipal by-law if any physical office, showroom, or warehouse premises are operated; register with the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and Compensation Fund through the Department of Employment and Labour upon commencement of employment; maintain the statutory company records at the registered office, including the minute book, share register, MOI, notices of registered office, and beneficial ownership register.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and registered MOI
Directors' ID copies and proof of residential address
FICA documentation including source of funds and beneficial ownership register
Lease or title deed evidencing physical trading/warehouse premises
SARS tax clearance or SARS registration confirmation
Signed board resolution appointing bank signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank rejects the account application for deficient FICA documents, file a supplementary directors' resolution and certified ID copies and resubmit; if a municipal trading licence objection is lodged, appeal to the Municipal Manager or file a reconsideration with the licensing authority; for late UIF/COIDA registration, registrations may be backdated upon submission of pay records, and penalties may be waived on a good-cause explanation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure marketplace FBA resale. If any manufacturing or product compliance activity is added, the competent authority would be the National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS) under the NRCS Act 5 of 2008 for compulsory specification (SABS/NRCS mark) matters; for general retail distribution, no industrial manufacturing permit is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license is required for an online marketplace reseller under ISIC 4791. A Municipal Business (Trading) Licence under the Business Act 71 of 1991 or local trading by-law applies only if the company operates a physical trading premises or dispatch warehouse within a municipal area.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) acting through provincial environmental authorities under NEMA 107 of 1998
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt category: pure online retail and distribution warehousing does not trigger a listed activity under EIA Regulations 2014 Listing Notices 1, 2 or 3 (GN 983, 984, 985 as amended); no environmental authorization or full EIA report is required. A general duty of care under section 28 of NEMA applies to prevent environmental degradation from packaging or waste operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge or atmospheric emission thresholds apply to a general FBA retail operation. If warehouse operations generate controlled waste (e.g., damaged goods, packaging, returns), the company must comply with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008, including waste classification, storage controls, and municipal waste stream separation, and must not emit VOCs or particulate matter unless industrial processes are added.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Required only where a physical office or warehouse is occupied: fire safety certificate from the local Fire Protection Services; electrical Certificate of Compliance (COC) under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993; SANS 10400 building occupancy clearance and structural load inspection for pallet racking or high-density shelving; general occupational health and safety compliance under OHSA 85 of 1993 with a risk assessment and a designated competent person; municipal zoning and health clearance for any customer-facing or inventory-holding premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); returns and registrations are filed via the SARS eFiling portal (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za); customs declarations are transmitted electronically to the SARS Customs Division via eFiling or approved EDI channels (SAD500 bill of entry).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP-1 Incorporation: register the (Pty) Ltd with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC); the integrated e-registration automatically allocates an Income Tax Reference Number (ITRN) and provisional-tax status, so a separate income-tax application is not required for a ZA-incorporated entity. STEP-2 Public officer: within one month of commencing business, appoint a South African resident 'public officer' responsible for tax compliance (Income Tax Act s65; Companies Act s33(4)) and file the appointment with SARS. STEP-3 VAT: apply for VAT registration via eFiling (VAT 101) where taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12-month period (compulsory within 21 days) or from ZAR 50,000 for voluntary registration. STEP-4 Customs: register as an importer/exporter through the SARS Customs 'Trader Registration' module to obtain a Customs Code (DA 185/eFiling), a prerequisite for cross-border stock movement and export bill-of-entry declaration. STEP-5 Exchange control: open a ZAR and/or foreign-currency account with an Authorised Dealer bank and comply with SARB reporting so that export proceeds are received and inward-receipt certificates are issued. STEP-6 PAYE/UIF: register for PAYE, SDL and UIF (EMP101e) within 21 days of becoming an employer if the FBA operation engages South African staff.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A ZA-incorporated (Pty) Ltd is automatically a South African tax resident (Income Tax Act s1: incorporation or place of effective management, subject to DTA tie-breaker) and is taxed at the corporate income tax rate of 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023) on worldwide income; no pass-through eligibility exists. The company is a separate VAT 'vendor' carrying on an enterprise in South Africa for the marketplace retail business (ISIC 4791) and cannot claim territorial scope or tax-exempt-zone treatment. Dividends paid are subject to a separate 20% dividends tax withheld at entity level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no U.S.-style 'check-the-box' election: entity classification follows statutory residence and source tests, not taxpayer choice. Available elections include: (i) voluntary VAT registration once turnover exceeds ZAR 50,000 (s23(2) VAT Act); (ii) discretionary VAT grouping of closely-held companies under s50A VAT Act (SARS consent required); (iii) election to apply the 'foreign business establishment' exclusion to exempt controlled foreign company income (s9D(9A) Income Tax Act); and (iv) the external-company branch election for non-resident entities (not applicable to a ZA (Pty) Ltd). Hybrid mismatch rules (s25H-s25N Income Tax Act, effective 1 January 2020, aligned with OECD BEPS Action 2) apply automatically by statutory ordering and cannot be elected away.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 compulsory threshold (taxable supplies made or expected to be made in any 12-month period; registration within 21 days of exceeding - s23(1) VAT Act); voluntary registration is permitted from ZAR 50,000 turnover (s23(2)). Non-resident suppliers of electronic services are separately registered under the FES regime from ZAR 50,000, but the ZA-resident (Pty) Ltd is subject to the standard ZAR 1,000,000 enterprise threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping or digital stamping of invoices is in force in South Africa. SARS eFiling is the statutory channel for VAT returns (two-monthly by default) and customs declarations (SAD500 bill of entry). A full tax invoice must contain the 15 particulars set out in s20(4) of the VAT Act and must state 'ZERO-RATED - EXPORT' where export zero-rating is claimed. SARS has published draft proposals for a phased PEPPOL-based mandatory e-invoicing regime (public consultation 2023-2024), but it is not yet law; vendors must retain electronic records for at least 5 years (VAT Act s55; Tax Administration Act s29).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies under s11(1)(a) where the registered vendor supplies movable goods and the goods are physically exported from South Africa within 90 days of the date of supply, provided the vendor carries on an enterprise, the export occurs through a SARS-designated port/airport, and the vendor holds the prescribed documentary proof including the VAT 264 export certificate (s54A VAT Act). Amazon FBA cross-border sales fulfilled from a South African fulfilment centre to non-resident consumers qualify if the export and payment-remittance conditions are met; stock transfers to a foreign Amazon centre without a sale are not taxable supplies, so zero-rating applies only at the point of an actual export sale. Services: s11(2)(l) zero-rates services supplied to a non-resident (not used in a South African business) and s11(2)(m) zero-rates services physically performed outside South Africa; offshore marketplace and fulfilment services consumed abroad qualify. A valid VAT 264 certificate, customs export declaration, and Inward Remittance Certificate must be in SARS's possession before an export refund is released.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SARS Customs Export Declaration (SAD500 electronic bill of entry through eFiling/TradeLink)
VAT 264 Export Certificate (SARS s54A verification-of-export form)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or Seaway Bill showing the South African port/airport of export
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an Authorised Dealer confirming receipt of foreign-currency export proceeds
Commercial tax invoice marked 'ZERO-RATED - EXPORT' with all s20(4) VAT particulars
Packing list, freight-forwarder delivery confirmation and port terminal receipt evidencing physical departure of goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS conducts real-time data matching between export bills of entry, VAT 264 certificates, FX inward-receipt records and VAT refund claims; refunds are automatically suspended for manual verification where the export bundle is incomplete. If zero-rated goods are not exported within 90 days or the VAT 264 certificate is not obtained, the zero-rating is reversed: output tax at 15% plus statutory interest (Tax Administration Act s187, prescribed rate, compounded monthly) is raised by additional assessment; the standard assessment window is 3 years, extended to 6 years for material non-disclosure (s99 TAA) and unlimited in fraud cases. Understatement penalties under s222/223 TAA range from 10% (standard case), 50% (substantial understatement), 75% (failure to take reasonable care), 100% (no reasonable grounds), 150% (gross negligence) to 200% (intentional tax evasion), stacking with interest and ad valorem penalties. Criminal prosecution for fraudulent export zero-rating claims under s234-235 TAA and s87 of the Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964 may result in fines up to ten times the tax involved and/or imprisonment of up to five years, with retrospective clawback of any refund already paid.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933, with parallel AML/CFT oversight by the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC). Authorised Dealers (licensed commercial banks) execute exchange control on SARB's behalf.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The ZAR is a floating, quasi-convertible currency. Current account items (trade in goods, e-commerce proceeds, commissions, dividends, interest) are freely convertible provided the underlying transaction is evidenced and the proceeds are repatriated within statutory deadlines. Capital account transactions (equity subscriptions, shareholder loans, quasi-capital funding, derivative settlement) require prior FinSurv approval or an Authorised Dealer notification under the Capital Flow Management framework. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted upon production of an auditor's certificate of distributable reserves, a SARS tax clearance or IT3(b) dividend declaration, and settlement of the 20% Dividends Withholding Tax (rate may be reduced under a double tax treaty). No general restriction applies to Amazon FBA sales receipts, but all USD/ZAR conversions must take place onshore through an Authorised Dealer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For Amazon FBA and direct e-commerce exports, the full sale consideration must be received in South Africa within 180 days of the shipment date (bill of lading or airway bill). Upon receipt in the ZA operating account or a Foreign Currency Account (FCA), the proceeds must be sold/converted to ZAR (surrendered) to an Authorised Dealer within 30 days, unless retained under the FCA export retention allowance (up to 100% for bona fide exporters with an export permit code). Every export transaction must be supported by a SARS customs declaration (SAD500), commercial invoice, and delivery evidence; conversion is executed at the ruling spot rate unless covered by a forward exchange contract.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account (Business Bundle)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: FirstRand Bank Limited (trading as First National Bank - FNB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account (Business Fusion)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account (Business Stream)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account (Nedbank Business Plus)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account (Private Banking)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with limited legal scope. Offshore digital EMIs (Airwallex, Stripe, Payoneer, Wise Business) are not SARB Authorised Dealers and cannot provide statutory ZAR clearing, convertibility, or exchange-control reporting. They may lawfully operate as non-bank payment facilitators under the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998 for collection of Amazon marketplace payouts in USD/EUR, but all repatriated funds MUST be routed to a South African Authorised Dealer for surrender and settlement. Stripe operates a licensed South African entity for local card acquiring; Airwallex and Payoneer may hold client funds offshore only. EMIs are therefore acceptable as collection-only rails, not as the primary treasury infrastructure. Their use triggers additional KYC documentation and may complicate the 180-day repatriation timeline if funds remain parked offshore.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA (Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001) mandates identification and verification of every director, beneficial owner, and signatory. For a ZA (Pty) Ltd with non-resident shareholders, at least one executive director or authorized signatory must attend a physical or equivalent remote interview at the chosen bank branch. Remote video onboarding is accepted for South African tax-resident directors who complete biometric verification, provided the company is fully CIPC-compliant. Non-resident directors may be verified remotely only if the bank accepts a notarised and apostilled copy of the passport plus a certified proof of residential address; in practice, major banks still require a one-time physical visit or a face-to-face meeting through a foreign correspondent bank for a full mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO holding shares through an opaque offshore structure (e.g., holding company in Cyprus, HK, or BVI) above the 25% ownership threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the CIPC issued company register, certificate of incorporation of all intermediate holding entities, full register of members, FIC-compliant UBO declaration (Guidance Note 7), source of wealth statement, 12-month global bank statements, and a notarised group structure summary identifying natural persons controlling the Amazon seller account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-ticket card sales profile with elevated chargebacks typical of marketplace retail (Amazon FBA).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide Amazon Seller Central settlement reports covering at least 3 months, net settlement amount summaries, refund and chargeback ratio below 1%, VAT/sales tax registration evidence, signed marketplace services agreement, and an explanatory memorandum on the FBA fulfilment model showing inventory shipment records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments or intermingled personal funds received into the business account from unrelated parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an affidavit from the directors explaining the payment flows, underlying sales orders and invoices, Amazon payout remittance advice, logistics proof (airway bills, customs entries), and counter-party identification documents for any third-party funder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to demonstrate export proceeds repatriation and ZAR conversion (exchange-control red flag for e-commerce exporters).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle SAD500 customs declarations, commercial invoices, bill of lading/airway bills, the Authorised Dealer's Exchange Control Form E / Form A, foreign currency account statements, forward exchange contract confirmations, and a reconciliation schedule matching Amazon settlements to bank credits.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholder equity injection: remit via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own bank account to the ZA (Pty) Ltd Capital Escrow Account held at an Authorised Dealer. The instruction must carry BOP purpose code 'Share Capital Subscription' and reference the board resolution approving the share issue. The Authorised Dealer files Exchange Control Form A and updates the share register; funds become freely usable for operating expenditure only after the bank's compliance release. No prior SARB approval is required for ordinary share capital, but the transaction is reported to FinSurv under the Capital Flow Management framework. If the funds arrive as a shareholder loan in excess of a 3:1 debt-to-equity ratio, prior SARB approval becomes mandatory. For Amazon FBA working capital, a combined 'share capital + subordinated loan' structure with a 70:30 equity bias is recommended to streamline conversion and future dividend repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails are executed through the Authorised Dealer network: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments, freight, customs duties, Amazon platform fees, and advertising costs, with BOP purpose codes referencing the underlying proforma invoice; (2) Commercial Letter of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700 for bulk inventory procurement, covering the exporter of record and shipping documents; (3) ZAR-denominated domestic legs settled through SAMOS (South African Multiple Option Settlement) using MT202 COV; (4) FCA-to-FCA transfers for same-currency payments without ZAR conversion. Gross settlement is mandatory - netting of Amazon payouts against supplier invoices is not permitted. All outward payments must be captured against the company's import permit and supported by SARS customs declarations to avoid exchange-control penalties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore Deliverable Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) with an Authorised Dealer, maximum tenor 12 months (renewable up to 24 months with FinSurv approval), to hedge USD/ZAR Amazon payout conversions

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) on ZAR executed through a non-resident counterparty, permissible for non-resident entities and for hedging ZAR exposure where onshore deliverability is impractical
Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) between USD and ZAR executed through an Authorised Dealer, subject to FinSurv approval for maturities exceeding 12 months
Zero-Cost Collar (Range Forward) combining a purchased USD call and a written USD put with an Authorised Dealer, permitted for risk management of forecast Amazon sales proceeds

Currency Options purchased (premium paid) onshore or offshore, treated as speculative only if the notional exceeds the underlying FBA receivables; prudential limits apply to keep the hedge in the ordinary course of trade

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) - electronic filing via eCIPC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation, every calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty per CIPC tariff; after two consecutive years of non-filing, CIPC may commence administrative strike-off under s82(3) of Companies Act 71 of 2008; company loses good-standing status and cannot obtain compliance certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership declaration and annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC through the annual return filing and BO Register submission on eCIPC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: With each annual return, within 30 business days after incorporation anniversary; changes to beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Filing of false, incomplete or late beneficial ownership information is a criminal offence; CIPC may impose administrative compliance actions, suspend filings, or strike off the company; directors may face personal accountability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and audit/review report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders (adoption); filed with CIPC when the company is a public company, state-owned company, or otherwise required to be audited; retained in statutory records in all cases
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Preparation and board approval within six months after financial year-end; shareholder adoption at the annual general meeting in accordance with the Memorandum of Incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence under the Companies Act; directors may be held liable; CIPC may compel filing where required; financial records remain subject to examination and may attract civil penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is mandatory under Companies Act 71 of 2008 for a public, state-owned or listed company, and for any other company whose Public Interest Score (PIS) is at least 500 in the financial year. PIS is calculated as 1 point per voting shareholder, 1 point per employee, 1 point per ZAR 1 million of third-party debt, and 1 point per ZAR 1 million of revenue. A company with a PIS of 100-499 is generally subject to independent review; below 100, compiled financial statements are permissible unless the Memorandum of Incorporation requires a higher standard.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS (IASB) for public companies, state-owned companies and audited companies; IFRS for SMEs is expressly permitted for eligible private companies; local South African GAAP is accepted only where law or prior practice permits for reporting periods before the IFRS transition.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must keep an accurate register of beneficial owners in its statutory records and confirm the register to CIPC as part of the annual return. The confirmation identifies each beneficial owner's full legal name, identity/registration number, nationality, residency/tax residence, nature and extent of beneficial interest. Any issuance, transfer or cancellation of interests resulting in a beneficial-ownership change must be recorded within 7 days and filed with CIPC within 30 days of the change. If no beneficial owner exists, a nil declaration must be filed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Debentures (if debentures are issued)
Minute Book (shareholder, director, and any audit committee minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 to USD 500 per annum for registered office service, statutory register maintenance and company secretarial support in South Africa
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 to USD 18,000 per annum for a full IFRS independent audit; USD 1,000 to USD 3,500 per annum for an independent review or compilation by an accredited accounting officer where no audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; 28% applied to earlier years
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Qualifying deductions include the section 11D research and development additional deduction, section 12B accelerated capital allowances for renewable energy assets, and the progressive Small Business Corporation rate schedule for qualifying close-held entities. E-commerce operating expenses are deductible if incurred in the production of income and supported by contemporaneous records.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited for an active trade carried on continuously; however, set-off of an assessed loss is limited to 80% of taxable income for years of assessment ending on or after 1 January 2019, and the loss lapses if the trade ceases.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 Company Income Tax Return filed through SARS eFiling; provisional tax payments are made on IRP6 returns via the SARS E-filing and banks.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final income tax return after financial year-end; provisional tax estimates due twice a year with a final top-up at year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ITR14 must be filed no later than 12 months after the financial year-end, unless SARS eFiling prescribes an earlier filing instruction. A company with a February financial year-end is ordinarily required to file by the end of the following January.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal registered name of ZA_PTY_LTD, CIPC registration number, SARS taxpayer reference number, registered address, and financial year-end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not complete this field. The Pty Ltd is the taxpayer and must file under its own name; if it is an external company branch, the South African branch details are used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross e-commerce sales arising from FBA transactions, reported before Amazon marketplace commissions, FBA fulfilment fees, shipping reimbursements, and refunds. South Africa-source rules may require inclusion of sales to South African customers where inventory is located in South Africa or the seller has a permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A South African-resident Pty Ltd must report worldwide FBA income. A non-resident seller without a South African permanent establishment reports only South Africa-source e-commerce income; export sales and deemed-source exceptions must be analyzed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses include cost of goods sold, Amazon selling fees, storage and fulfilment charges, freight, advertising, payment-processing fees, and administrative overheads, provided they are actually incurred for the production of income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident head-office charges are deductible only under the arm's length and transfer pricing rules; invoices from Amazon or related entities must be substantiated and reflect actual services and allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Set-off of prior year assessed loss against current-year taxable income, subject to the continuity of the same trade and the 80% taxable income limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident may not offset South African branch losses against offshore income; for the Pty Ltd, the loss must have arisen while carrying on the same trade that remains active.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by 27%, after allowances and deductions, then reduced by rebates and prepayments. Dividend withholding tax, VAT, and PAYE liabilities are not entered here.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax payable belongs to the Pty Ltd; dividends declared to foreign owners are not deductible and trigger dividend withholding tax separately.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative non-compliance penalty under section 210 of the Tax Administration Act, generally from ZAR 250 to ZAR 16,000 per month depending on taxable turnover. Underpayment of provisional tax attracts interest at the prescribed rate plus a 10% to 20% penalty, and an understatement penalty may rise to 150% or 200% of the shortfall.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% on dividends declared and paid by a South African resident company to its shareholders, subject to exemptions and applicable double taxation agreement (DTA) reductions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A foreign shareholder seeking DTA relief must submit a valid declaration of beneficial ownership and a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home tax authority before the dividend is paid. The Pty Ltd, as withholding agent, applies the reduced treaty rate only after receiving the declaration and supporting TRC in SARS eFiling; if 20% is withheld, the foreign shareholder may apply to SARS for a refund by showing treaty entitlement and substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on South Africa-source royalties paid to non-residents is 15%; statutory withholding on South Africa-source interest is 15%. DTA rates may be reduced to 0%, 5%, 10%, or 15% depending on the treaty, beneficial ownership, and submission of a TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No fixed statutory Local File / Master File threshold applies to all affected transactions, but ITR14 disclosure is triggered when annual affected transactions with connected persons exceed ZAR 1,000,000. Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must be maintained for all material cross-border affected transactions; SARS prioritizes cases where the annual aggregate transaction value exceeds ZAR 100,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations filing regime. The enquiry is applied through the residence test, effective-management determination, controlled foreign corporation rules, section 31 transfer pricing, and the general anti-avoidance rules. A Pty Ltd must maintain real commercial substance, local decision-making, board minutes, employment, and bank accounts to support tax residence, DTA access, and arm's length pricing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-reporting Amazon FBA sales, inflating deductions for FBA fees, or submitting false ITR14 schedules and financial statements to SARS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under section 234 of the Tax Administration Act, making a false declaration is an offence punishable by a fine and/or imprisonment for a period not exceeding two years. The evasion penalty can include an understatement penalty of up to 200% of the shortfall plus interest, and a criminal conviction may follow under common-law fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the corporate veil if the Pty Ltd is used fraudulently or as an alter ego. Directors who knowingly participate in false tax returns may be held jointly liable for the company's unpaid tax, receive travel bans and preservation orders, and face imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company or Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: ZA_PTY_LTD is used as a bare holding shell, with no employees, local bank account, office, or board meetings, while foreign directors attempt to shift profits offshore or claim treaty benefits on passive e-commerce income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may disregard the juristic personality, recharacterize the arrangement under sections 80A-80L, include profits in the shareholder's hands under CFC rules, deny treaty relief, and impose an understatement penalty up to 150% or 200% of the tax shortfall.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable under section 77 of the Companies Act for carrying on business recklessly or knowingly as a shell, with remedies including civil restitution, disqualification from acting as directors, and travel bans for unpaid SARS debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Artificial Related-party Fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's length management royalties, excessive marketing fees, or inflated FBA-related service fees to the South African company, or eroding South African taxable income through circular cross-border payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may adjust the taxable income to an arm's length amount under section 31, disallow the deduction, and assess interest plus an understatement penalty of 100% to 150% for substantial misstatements. Failure to retain the required documentation can itself attract an administrative penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs the return knowing the transfer pricing policy is artificial can be joined in the assessment under the Tax Administration Act, with personal liability for the shortfall, interest, and penalties, and potential criminal prosecution for deliberate misstatement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Pty Ltd conceals the identity of non-resident beneficial owners, accepts settlement proceeds through unverified payment rails, or processes Amazon FBA disbursements without maintaining a full customer and beneficial-ownership identification record under South African financial surveillance laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 imposes administrative fines up to ZAR 10,000,000 on accountable institutions and directors for serious non-compliance, in addition to criminal penalties for money laundering and possible liquidation proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers responsible for AML compliance face personal fines and imprisonment up to 15 years for knowingly enabling money laundering or failing to report suspicious transactions; corporate veil-piercing and civil recovery may also apply.
